sections.skill: Identify major taxes and classify taxes as progressive, regressive, or proportional

questions.prompt: Which tax is charged when you buy a taxable item at a store?
questions.intro: Governments collect several kinds of taxes: income taxes on earnings (federal and most states), payroll taxes for Social Security and Medicare, sales taxes on purchases (state and local), property taxes on real estate (local), and excise taxes on specific goods such as gasoline.
questions.feedback: Sales tax is charged on purchases.
questions.topic: Types of taxes and how they work
sources: New Jersey Division of Taxation (Income tax): New Jersey has a state income tax (Form NJ-1040) with graduated rates. (https://www.nj.gov/treasury/taxation/njit25.shtml)

questions.prompt: Under a PROGRESSIVE tax, what happens as income rises?

choices.text: The same percentage is paid at every income level
A smaller percentage is paid in tax
A larger percentage of income is paid in tax
Everyone pays the same dollar amount

questions.correct_answer: A larger percentage of income is paid in tax
questions.intro: A progressive tax takes a larger percentage from higher incomes (the federal income tax). A proportional ("flat") tax takes the same percentage from everyone. A regressive tax takes a larger percentage of income from lower incomes, for example a sales tax on necessities.
questions.feedback: Progressive taxes rise as a share of income when income rises.
questions.topic: Types of taxes and how they work
sources: New Jersey Division of Taxation (Income tax): New Jersey has a state income tax (Form NJ-1040) with graduated rates. (https://www.nj.gov/treasury/taxation/njit25.shtml)

questions.prompt: Two people each buy $500 of taxable goods with a 6% sales tax. One earns $25,000 a year; the other earns $250,000. What percent of income does each pay in this tax?
questions.intro: To see whether a tax is regressive, compare the tax paid with each person's income.
questions.feedback: Tax: $500 × 0.06 = $30 each. $30 ÷ $25,000 = 0.12%; $30 ÷ $250,000 = 0.012%. The lower earner pays a larger share, so this is regressive.
questions.topic: Types of taxes and how they work

misconceptions.B: Assumes the tax depends on income
